title: From Untrusted Input to Trusted Memory: A Systematic Study of Memory Poisoning Attacks in LLM Agents
claims_used: The study identifies multiple memory-write channels and structural vulnerabilities, introduces a taxonomy and MPBench, and reports that systems designed to write and retrieve memory more aggressively can become more exploitable. The manuscript uses it to frame memory security as a write-retrieve-act pipeline rather than a single filtering problem.
caveat: This is a preprint rather than a peer-reviewed conference or journal paper as of the cited date.
